subject: paediatrics
title: Classic Cardiac Silhouettes: Egg-on-String and Snowman TAPVC

steps.tx: Pathological alterations in cardiac chamber architecture and great vessel alignment generate recognizable **characteristic cardiac silhouettes** on plain chest radiography. Frontal radiography provides an indispensable bedside screening tool in cyanotic neonates, where specific cardiac contours reflect underlying embryological misalignments. Well-defined radiographic patterns include the narrow mediastinal pedicle of transposed great arteries, the supracardiac figure-of-eight contour of anomalous pulmonary venous return, and the upturned cardiac apex of tetralogy.
steps.say: Distinctive cardiac silhouettes on chest X-rays reveal underlying congenital heart anomalies. The egg-on-a-string pattern signals TGA, while the snowman appearance indicates TAPVC.

vis.alt: Frontal chest radiographs demonstrating classic cardiac silhouettes in cyanotic heart diseases.
vis.caption: Radiographic comparison of egg-on-string TGA, snowman TAPVC, and boot-shaped TOF silhouettes. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Anterior-posterior alignment of transposed vessels and thymic involution produce a distinctive mediastinal silhouette. In transposition of the great arteries, chest radiography demonstrates the classic **egg on a string silhouette**, characterized by an enlarged, oval, globular cardiac contour (the egg) paired with a strikingly narrow superior mediastinal vascular pedicle (the string). Increased pulmonary vascular markings reflect pulmonary plethora.
steps.say: The egg-on-a-string appearance in TGA combines an enlarged oval heart with a narrow mediastinal pedicle. The aorta sitting directly anterior to the pulmonary artery narrows the shadow.

left.title: Narrow Mediastinal Pedicle (The String)
points: Aorta lies directly anterior to pulmonary artery
Great vessels superimpose in AP view, narrowing pedicle
Stress-induced thymic atrophy narrows upper shadow

right.title: Globular Cardiac Base (The Egg)
points: Right ventricular and left ventricular volume enlargement
Egg-shaped oval contour lying on left diaphragm
Prominent pulmonary vascular plethora across lungs

steps.tx: Failure of pulmonary veins to join the left atrium redirects all pulmonary venous return into systemic veins. The anomaly termed **total anomalous pulmonary venous connection** (TAPVC) occurs when all four pulmonary veins fail to connect directly to the left atrium, instead draining anomalously into the right atrium or systemic venous tributaries. The right atrium receives both systemic and pulmonary venous blood, requiring an interatrial communication for systemic cardiac output.
steps.say: Total anomalous pulmonary venous connection drains all pulmonary veins into systemic venous circulation. Oxygenated and deoxygenated blood mix entirely in the right atrium.

rows: Left vertical vein -> Innominate vein -> SVC
Drains directly into coronary sinus or RA
Descending vein through diaphragm -> Portal vein/IVC

steps.tx: Dilated supracardiac venous conduits superimpose above the heart to create a two-tiered silhouette. In supracardiac TAPVC, chest radiography demonstrates the classic **snowman heart figure of 8**, where a wide upper mediastinal shadow sits atop an enlarged globular heart. The upper circle of the snowman is formed by the dilated left vertical vein, horizontal left innominate vein, and dilated superior vena cava carrying massive pulmonary blood flow.
steps.say: Supracardiac TAPVC generates the snowman or figure-of-eight sign on chest X-rays. Dilated vertical and innominate veins form the upper head, resting on an enlarged cardiac body.

left.title: Upper Mediastinal Loop (Snowman Head)
points: Dilated left vertical vein on the left
Engorged horizontal innominate vein across top
Massive superior vena cava on the right

right.title: Lower Cardiac Silhouette (Snowman Body)
points: Right atrial and right ventricular dilatation
Normal-sized left atrium and left ventricle
Prominent active pulmonary plethora throughout lung fields

steps.tx: Subdiaphragmatic venous passage creates severe mechanical compression and acute pulmonary edema. In infracardiac TAPVC, the common pulmonary venous channel traverses the diaphragm through the oesophageal hiatus to join the portal vein or ductus venosus, precipitating **infracardiac TAPVC obstruction**. Compression by the diaphragm and constriction of hepatic sinusoids trigger acute pulmonary venous hypertension, severe pulmonary edema, ground-glass lung fields, and refractory hypoxaemia mimicking respiratory distress syndrome.
steps.say: Infracardiac TAPVC veins traverse the diaphragm, becoming severely compressed. High pulmonary venous pressure causes acute pulmonary edema with ground-glass X-rays, requiring emergency surgery.

rows: Obstructed TAPVC is an extreme emergency
Small heart with severe pulmonary edema
Large heart with snowman sign and plethora
Normal or mildly elevated pulmonary pressure

steps.tx: Complete intracardiac mixing at the right atrial level equalizes chamber oxygen saturation. In unobstructed TAPVC, **interatrial mixing physiology** produces nearly identical oxygen saturation values across all four cardiac chambers, typically between eighty-five and ninety percent. Blood flow to the pulmonary bed is four to five times higher than systemic output, resulting in mild clinical cyanosis masked by severe tachypnoea and progressive right heart failure.
steps.say: Complete mixing in the right atrium equalizes oxygen saturations across all four chambers. High pulmonary blood flow causes mild cyanosis with tachypnoea and right heart failure.

left.title: Haemodynamic Saturation Profile
points: Right atrium receives all venous blood
Saturation in RA, RV, LA, and LV is identical (88%)
Mild cyanosis often missed clinically in nursery

right.title: Auscultatory Physical Signs
points: Wide fixed split S2 sound (similar to ASD)
Systolic ejection murmur at pulmonary area
Mid-diastolic tricuspid flow rumble
Marked right ventricular parasternal heave

steps.tx: Surgical redirection of pulmonary venous flow establishes anatomical series circulation. Definitive management of TAPVC requires **surgical pulmonary venous anastomosis**, where the common pulmonary venous confluence is anastomosed directly to the posterior wall of the left atrium. The anomalous vertical vein or descending channel is ligated, and the obligate atrial septal defect is closed with a pericardial patch to restore separate systemic and pulmonary circulations.
steps.say: Surgical repair connects the pulmonary venous confluence directly into the left atrium, ligates anomalous draining veins, and closes the atrial septal defect.

rows: Diverts pulmonary venous flow into LA
Must ensure adequate LA compliance first
Separates right and left atrial chambers
Left atrial line and pulmonary arterial monitoring
Inhaled nitric oxide for pulmonary hypertension

steps.tx: Serial echocardiographic evaluation monitors for late anastomotic narrowing and pulmonary hypertension. Following repair, patients require lifelong surveillance for **postoperative pulmonary venous stenosis**, a fibromuscular narrowing of the surgical anastomosis occurring in up to ten percent of cases. Recurrent stenosis manifests with progressive dyspnoea, haemoptysis, and recurrent pulmonary hypertension, requiring transcatheter balloon angioplasty, cutting balloon dilation, stenting, or sutureless reoperation.
steps.say: Postoperative anastomotic narrowing occurs in ten percent of cases, causing recurrent pulmonary hypertension. Serial echocardiography detects stenosis, treatable by balloon angioplasty or stenting.

left.title: Anastomotic Stenosis Warning Signs
points: Recurrent exertional tachypnoea and cough
Doppler mean gradient across anastomosis >4 mmHg
Loss of phasic pulmonary venous Doppler flow
Unilateral or bilateral pulmonary venous hypertension

right.title: Therapeutic Catheter Options
points: High-pressure balloon angioplasty dilation
Cutting balloon disruption of fibrotic scar
Intravascular stent implantation across veins
Sutureless pericardial pouch reoperation
